resources.string: Your Synapse server at a glance: who\'s signed in, health and what needs attention.
Add your Synapse server to get started.
SynapseCtrl is free and open source. Sponsor development on GitHub
Found a problem or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub

Enter the address of your Synapse server and sign in with an account that is a server admin. If /_synapse/admin is only open on your network, use Synapse\'s LAN address, like http://192.168.1.20:8008.
Connects to %1$s, and only to this address
Without http://, SynapseCtrl uses HTTPS. SynapseCtrl only ever connects to the address you enter here.
That doesn\'t look like a web address.
Plain http:// is only allowed for addresses on your own network (like 192.168.x.x or synapse.lan), because SynapseCtrl sends your admin access token with every request. Use https:// for this address.
Defaults to the server name, like vkhub.org
Allow plain HTTP for this server
Your admin access token travels unencrypted on your network
Only for addresses on your own network. A name like synapse.lan must also point to a private address, or SynapseCtrl won\'t connect. HTTPS is safer.

SynapseCtrl will talk to %1$s without encryption. Every request carries your admin access token, which can do anything on your server, so anyone who can watch your network could take it over. Only do this on a network you trust.
%1$s uses a certificate your phone doesn\'t know, like a self-signed certificate.
%1$s now presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. Only continue if you replaced or renewed it yourself.
Check that this SHA-256 fingerprint matches your certificate (on the server: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256):
From now on SynapseCtrl only accepts this exact certificate from this server.
Switch, add or remove Synapse servers
SynapseCtrl logs its access token out on the server (so it stops working there too), then forgets this server and deletes the token from the phone. Nothing else changes on the server.
Hide every action that changes something on this server, and refuse to send one
Can\'t reach %1$s. Check the address and that your phone is on a network that can reach it.
%1$s presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. SynapseCtrl stopped connecting to protect your access token.
Wrong username or password, or the server refused the login.
%1$s answered with a redirect. SynapseCtrl never follows redirects, so enter the address Synapse actually answers on (often its https:// address).
%1$s redirects to %2$s. SynapseCtrl never follows redirects, so enter that address instead (often the https:// one).
SynapseCtrl won\'t use plain HTTP for %1$s: it\'s only allowed for addresses on your own network, with the server\'s HTTP switch on.
SynapseCtrl only connects to the servers you added, so this request wasn\'t sent.
This server is in read-only mode, so nothing was changed. Turn read-only mode off to make changes.
Cancelled: the change wasn\'t confirmed with your fingerprint or app PIN, so nothing was sent.

Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening SynapseCtrl. While locked, your admin access tokens stay encrypted with the PIN and nothing is sent to your servers, unless you turned on background checks
SynapseCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your own Synapse servers.

Background checks are on, so they can still reach your servers while SynapseCtrl is locked: your admin access tokens are then only encrypted with the Android Keystore, as without the app lock. Turn off background checks in Notifications to keep them sealed with your PIN too. SynapseCtrl has no analytics or tracking.
Screenshots and screen recordings show a blank screen
The recent apps view shows a blank card instead of the app
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Too many tries. Try again in %1$d s

The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it encrypts your saved access tokens. SynapseCtrl will remove every server with its token. The tokens stay valid on the server until you log them out there (for example from the admin account\'s session list). Nothing else changes on your servers.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to add your servers again.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
At least %1$d digits, separate from your phone\'s PIN
Enter your app PIN to turn the lock off.
Too easy to guess. Try a less obvious PIN.
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Couldn\'t save the PIN. Try again.
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first
As soon as you leave the app
Ask for your fingerprint or app PIN before anything that changes a server: users, invites, rooms, media and reports. Once confirmed, the next minute doesn\'t ask again
SynapseCtrl is about to change something on your server
SynapseCtrl is about to change something on your server. Enter your app PIN or use your fingerprint.
Background checks, push through ntfy, what to notify about
Notifications are blocked: tap to allow them

Synapse can\'t send notifications itself, so SynapseCtrl checks your servers in the background and tells you when something needs a look. Push through ntfy can start that check at once. The checks only read; nothing changes on your servers.
Notifications are blocked for SynapseCtrl, so the background checks can\'t tell you anything.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. They only talk to your own Synapse servers. With the app lock on, your admin access tokens stay usable in the background while these checks are on (see Privacy and security).
Last check %1$s couldn\'t reach the server
More events (new reports, health checks, media storage, new users) come in a later version.
Two checks in a row couldn\'t reach Synapse, or its access token or admin access stopped working
SynapseCtrl may run in the background
Battery optimisation can delay or skip checks

On ColorOS (OPPO, OnePlus) and other phones that close background apps aggressively: open SynapseCtrl\'s app info, then under Battery choose Allow background activity (or Don\'t optimise), and allow Auto launch if your phone has it.
Problems that need a look right away
Things worth knowing that need no action
Something on your Synapse server needs a look. Unlock to see it.
Runs the background check right away whenever something posts to SynapseCtrl\'s push address

Synapse can\'t push anything itself. Turn this on, copy the push address and let something on your network post to it, like a cron job. Every push makes SynapseCtrl check your servers at once, at most once a minute; what the message says is ignored. The regular background checks keep running as well.
ntfy isn\'t installed. Push comes only through the ntfy app: install it, connect it to your ntfy server, then come back here. Background checks work without it.
Turn on Check in the background too: a push only starts that check.
ntfy couldn\'t register SynapseCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then try again.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. The push address stays the same and background checks keep running.
Tap to copy. Treat this address like a password: anyone who has it can make SynapseCtrl check your servers (it never changes anything on them).
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so pushes arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s app info and set Battery to Unrestricted.
Local accounts: create, reset passwords, admins, devices, deactivate.
Rooms on your server: members, block, delete.
Storage per user, cleaning up local and remote media, quarantine.
SynapseCtrl is being built in stages. This version signs in and checks admin access; each update adds the next part.
Server counts, health checks (well-known, federation, calls) and what needs attention
Search and manage local users: create accounts, reset passwords, admin rights, devices, shadow-ban and deactivate. Invites with registration tokens come with it.
Every room on your server with its members, and blocking, making yourself room admin and deleting rooms.
Storage per user, purging cached remote media, deleting old or large local media, and quarantine.
Reported events with what was reported, and the federation destinations your server talks to.
Used once to log in: SynapseCtrl gets its own access token and never stores the password
Leave empty to keep the current sign-in
From an admin account. It will be logged out when you remove this server, so don\'t paste the token your chat app uses.
On: nothing can be changed from this phone
Read-only mode hides every write action and refuses to send one, even if a screen still shows it.
%1$s was removed, but its access token couldn\'t be logged out on the server. Log it out there yourself (the \"SynapseCtrl (Android)\" device of your admin account).
The access token doesn\'t work any more (logged out or expired). Sign in again.
This account isn\'t a server admin. Make it one on the server (see the README), or sign in with an admin account.
%1$s answers, but not on /_synapse/admin (HTTP %2$d). If you restricted the admin API to your network, use Synapse\'s LAN address here, like http://192.168.1.20:8008.
%1$s doesn\'t offer password login (it may use single sign-on or Matrix Authentication Service). Paste an access token from an admin account instead.
%1$s answered, but not like Synapse. Check the address: it should be where Synapse itself answers.
Not found: it may have been deleted already.
Synapse is rate-limiting these requests. Wait a moment and try again.
